question: Should OpenClaw retain `openclaw/plugin-sdk/test-state` as a documented repo-local test seam for first-party extension tests, rather than keep Telegram-specific state setup or introduce a published Plugin SDK contract?
rationale: The code makes a cross-boundary test helper available to bundled extensions while intentionally excluding it from ordinary builds and npm packaging; choosing that long-term ownership boundary is maintainer intent rather than a mechanical correctness question.

options.title: Keep the local test seam
options.body: Confirm the source-only helper as the canonical first-party extension-test path and preserve its package exclusions and boundary checks.

options.title: Keep state setup Telegram-local
options.body: Avoid a shared SDK-named seam by reverting the state-fixture portion of the consolidation and retaining extension-local test setup.

recommendation.title: Keep the local test seam
recommendation.body: Confirm the source-only helper as the canonical first-party extension-test path and preserve its package exclusions and boundary checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The available commit sequence shows this contributor carried the test-harness and repo-local seam design, although broader current-main ownership history could not be independently inspected.
